struck: When an insured part of a condo building is damaged, the association must repair it promptly.
use: When a part of a condo building the association must insure is damaged, the association must repair it promptly, unless repair is illegal or 80 percent of owners vote not to rebuild.

pattern: is what arrives as a special assessment
struck: That remainder is what arrives as a special assessment.
use: That shortfall can arrive as a special assessment.

struck: Engineers had found corroded reinforcing steel and a building envelope that was not weather tight.
use: A consultant found corroded reinforcing steel and a building envelope that was not weather tight.

struck: In 2008 the board proposed a special assessment of $88,398 per unit in Buildings A and B.
use: In 2009 the board proposed a special assessment of $88,398 per unit in Buildings A and B.

struck: The board then put the repair costs into the next two years' operating budgets, about half in each, so owners paid through their regular bills instead.
use: The board then put the repair costs into the 2010 and 2011 operating budgets instead, about half in 2010 and the rest planned for 2011.

struck: So a bigger or more valuable unit pays a bigger share of every assessment.
use: So a unit with a higher percentage pays more of every assessment.

struck: It cannot be changed without the agreement of every unit's owner.
use: It cannot be changed without every owner's agreement, except as a phased condo's master deed provides or when owners vote not to rebuild a unit.

struck: Owner decisions need a majority of at least 51 percent at a meeting.
use: Owner decisions need a majority of at least 51 percent, counted by the units' value percentages, not by heads.

struck: The master deed, covenants and bylaws are the only limits.
use: The limits on a special assessment are in the master deed, covenants and bylaws.

struck: No state cap, no required reserve study, no required inspection.
use: South Carolina's condo and HOA laws set no cap on a special assessment, require no reserve study and require no periodic structural inspection. The one report they require is an engineer's or architect's condition report when apartments are converted to condos.

pattern: passed the planning life of its roof
struck: A building built before 1990 has passed the planning life of its roof, its elevator machinery and its aluminum windows at least once.
use: A building built before 1990 has passed HUD's planning life for a flat or shingle roof, elevator machinery and aluminum windows at least once.

struck: Fannie Mae, whose rules most condo loans follow, lists items such as sea walls.
use: (cut the clause: no source says most condo loans follow Fannie Mae's rules)

pattern: owners whose units were damaged pay
struck: If a building is not insured, or the insurance does not cover the rebuilding, the owners whose units were damaged pay the rest in proportion to their units' value, unless the bylaws say otherwise.
use: Repair costs beyond the insurance and the reserve are shared by owners, by the master deed percentages or as the bylaws say.

struck: An association organized as a nonprofit corporation must keep minutes of every board and owners' meeting for good, and an owner may inspect them with five business days' written notice.
use: An owner may inspect and copy the last three years of owners' meeting minutes with five business days' written notice; for board minutes the owner must also give a proper purpose and name the records.

struck: Before a contract on a home in an association, South Carolina's disclosure addendum asks the seller.
use: In most resales, before a contract, the seller of a home in an association fills in the state's disclosure addendum.

pattern: no Fannie Mae loan|Fannie Mae loan can be made
struck: If it pays for a critical repair that has not been fixed, no Fannie Mae loan can be made in the building.
use: If it pays for a critical repair that has not been fixed, Fannie Mae will not buy a loan on any unit in the building.

pattern: inspection from the last (3|three) years must be read
struck: A structural or mechanical inspection from the last 3 years must be read.
use: If a structural or mechanical inspection was done in the last 3 years, the lender must get and read it.

struck: When a mortgage lender takes a unit at foreclosure, it does not owe the assessments that went unpaid before it took title.
use: When a mortgage lender, or anyone, buys a unit at the foreclosure sale of a recorded mortgage, it does not owe the unit's unpaid assessments that came due between the recording of that mortgage and the day it took title.

struck: An association organized as a nonprofit corporation may borrow money and pledge its income, which is how some boards spread a big repair over years of higher dues instead of one bill.
use: An association that is a nonprofit corporation may borrow money and pledge its income, unless its articles say otherwise.

struck: In 2025, 548 associations in Horry County recorded a lien against at least one owner for unpaid assessments, the most in any year since 2010.
use: In 2025, more than 500 associations in Horry County recorded a lien against at least one owner for unpaid charges, about the same as in 2024 and up from about 350 in 2021.

struck: 548 associations recorded a lien in 2025, up from 359 in 2021.
use: More than 500 associations recorded a lien in 2025, up from about 350 in 2021.

struck: Leaving out timeshare resorts and other bulk filers, associations recorded 1,536 such liens in 2025, about twice the 783 of 2021.
use: (cut it: the rise in the lien count depends on how bulk filers are cut, from 1.2 to 2 times)

struck: Your own condo policy may carry loss assessment coverage, which can pay a share of some assessments.
use: What your own condo policy covers is on our master insurance page.

struck: And they doubled in a year.
use: Complaints in Horry County disputing fees or special assessments more than doubled from 2024 to 2025, from 12 to 30.
